Similarly, although both DXA and CT scans were able to detect significant increases in thigh mass over a 10-week strength training program, a potentially meaningful difference of approximately 2 kg (4.4 lb) was noted between methods. Other research lends support to these findings (20). The discrepancies between single-point measures and those taken over the course of a longitudinal training study are likely caused by confounding from variations in adipose tissue or skin mass over time, which alters how the DXA algorithm determines lean mass (51).
